JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 09.01.2024 at about 9.00 a.m., when the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian at the road side near Kalyanai Motors, Opposite Srinivasapura Gate, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that point of time the 3 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-5211 drove it in a rash & negligent manner with high speed and dashed to deceased.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down on the road and sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Dobbaspet, wherein he took first aid and then shifted Government Hospital,
Tumkur, wherein he was admitted and during the course of treatment he died at the hospital.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, and was doing agriculture and earning Rs.30,000/- p.a.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of car and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of Private car policy in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-5211.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Non- compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6),
159 of MV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence,
mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

It is contended that the respondent No.1 had been willfully committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy by allowing to use their private own car for commercial purpose for carrying the passengers for hire purpose by attaching their vehicle through online Zoom App application services.
Therefore the insured has been prosecuted by the police as accused No.2 and Zoom App Manager / Venkatesh as Accused as No.3 for the offence punishable u/s 192(A) of M.V.Act.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its offending car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the accident took place due to the 5 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 negligence of the deceased as he tried to cross the NH road where there is no provision for crossing National Highway by pedestrian and invited to cause Gangaraju vs Jagannatha K R on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64126514/
2 the accident.
Hence he is the main architect for the unfortunate accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid driving licence as on the date of accident.

Thus it is clear breach of terms and conditions of the police and also violation of Section 150(2) of Amended M.V.Act-2009, therefore the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the first respondent in the above matter.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the 2 nd respondent is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
6 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.01.2024 at about 9.00 a.m., near Kalyanai Motors, opposite to Srinivasapura Gate, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH- 48 road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District due to actionable negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-5211 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 17 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 got examined its Associate Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 :

The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in Gangaraju vs Jagannatha K R on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64126514/
3 dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending car.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.
10. Mr.Venkatesh set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.14) against 8 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 the driver of car for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC and also filed against the owner u/s 192(A) of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

11. Further more the careful perusal of Ex.P.3 and 5 being Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch it reflects that the accident happened when the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian near Kalyanai Motors,
opposite to Srinivasapura Gate, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District.
It is further shows that the accident occured on the edge of the road i.e., opposite to Kalyani Motors Show room.
If the driver of car was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Further the IO has issued notice u/s 133 of MV Act as per Ex.P.8 & 11, the driver of the offending vehicle has replied to the notice u/s 133 of IMV Act, as per Ex.P.9 & 12.
The driver of the offending vehicle himself admitted that due to his rash and negligent act, accident occurred.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of the offending car.
This Court is 9 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.

But having regard to the Ex.P.3 &
5 which were read in consonance with the Ex.P.14 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash & negligent act of the driver of the car.
12. The respondent No.2 who denied negligence on the part of the driver of car and contended that the deceased had contributed to the accident, have not led any evidence to this effect.
Mere taking up of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the evidence led by the petitioners.
Further the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of the car who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the driver of the car is fatal to the defence of the respondents.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-5211.

Therefore, I answer issue No.2 as 'In the Affirmative.

14. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

sentences.text:
In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, 12 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

The petitioners contended that, 13 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 deceased was working as agriculturist and coolie and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-

5 p.a.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 14 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 09.01.2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

16. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P15 wherein the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1960, which indicates that he was aged (64 years 0 months 8 days) 64 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '7'.
17.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 64 years.
His income is taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects (as he was aged more than 60 years).
The deceased died living behind 2 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,000/- p.m. (Rs.16,500 - Rs.5,500 = Rs.11,000/-).
18. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of 15 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 dependency comes to Rs.9,24,000/- (Rs.11,000 X 12 X 7).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.9,24,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

19. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

The controversy is with regard to the liability of the Insurance Company in the matter of indemnification on the ground that the respondent No.1 willfully committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy by allowing to use their private own car for commercial purpose for carrying passengers for hire purpose by attaching their vehicle through on line Zoom-App application services.
Therefore the insured has been prosecuted by the police as Accused No.2 and Zoom App- Manager / Venkatesh is made as Accused No.3 under Section 192(A) of MV. Act.
Further it is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 150(2) of Amended M.V.Act 2009.

Therefore respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

On perusal of Dreamplug Advisory Solutions Private Limited (DASPL) works as a corporate agent, primarily facilitating insurance.
They offer insurance products and services, and their registered office is in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
The company also offers partner programs and financial assistance.

DASPL Finance simplifies insurance by offering customized products,
affordable pricing, and claim assistance.
Further DASPL acts as a bridge between insurance 19 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 companies and customers, helping individuals find and purchase insurance products.
The same company connected the owner of the vehicle to Zoom company app.
26. The advocate for petitioner argued that at the time of accident there was no passengers in the car and car was not used for commercial purpose during the accident.
It is relevant to note here that on careful perusal of the charge sheet at the time of accident there was no passengers in the car.
It clears that at the time of accident car was not used for commercial purpose though it was connected with zoom app.

It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Kalim Khan vs Fimidabee reported in 2018 (7) SCC 687. wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that "use of motor vehicle", includes non traffic use.

entities.text: Kalim Khan vs Fimidabee reported in 2018 (7) SCC 687
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The casual relationship should exist between violation and the accident cause.
There has to be some act done by the person concerned in causing the accident.

The commission or omission must have some nexus with the accident, though the "use" of the Motor vehicle concerned need not have an intimate and direct nexus 20 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 with the accident.
In such circumstances the claim is maintainable and insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
In the present case also it is contended that vehicle was used for commercial purpose.
But the use of vehicle does not necessary have to the immediate cause of accident, but it must be factor in the chain of evidence leading to the accident.

In the present case though in the charge sheet is contended that it was connected with zoom app even though it was private car and used for commercial purpose but at the time of accident there was no passengers in the car and thus it was not used for commercial purpose during the accident.
Even though it was used for commercial purpose, the accident is accident.
As per the documents accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the car.
Therefor in view of the above decision the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

27. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-5211 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the 21 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,40,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the 22 SCCH-23 MVC-1159/2024 compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 50%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
